summary: Implement a crash-consistent and private M10 durable v2 format while retaining strict read-only compatibility for legacy v1 payload+meta pairs. New committed state is one self-describing `*.checkpoint.json` envelope with bounded header + raw checkpoint bytes, written through a random exclusive mode-0600 temp file, fsynced, and atomically renamed as the single commit point. Invalid existing state fails closed before user code, and symlinks/non-regular entries are rejected by lstat-based checks.

pointers: readDurable fail-closed v2 + legacy v1 compatibility
corrupt and schema mismatch typed failures
M10 schema mismatch updated to v2 envelope

steps: Captured executable RED evidence in Actions run 34019230528: all four new durable-integrity cases failed on the old pair format while the existing suite stayed green.

The first guarded GREEN runner intentionally did not commit because TypeScript typecheck caught a generator escaping bug. The generator was corrected to preserve `\n` source escapes; no failed production candidate reached the branch.

Second guarded workflow 34019464960 applied the exact durable block, passed git diff check and TypeScript typecheck, passed the four focused #71/#83 tests and the existing M10 regression slice, then and only then committed production candidate 51d6474; temporary patch script/workflow were removed from the committed tree.

evidence.note: Expected RED: corrupt/version-incompatible durable state was treated as absence, umask(0) produced 0666 checkpoint files, and a planted predictable temp symlink redirected checkpoint bytes outside durableRoot.
Patch guard, git diff --check, pnpm typecheck, focused durable-integrity suite, existing M10 regression slice, and verified commit/push all passed.
Final diff contains only runtime/tests/package/development-memory; temporary patch script and workflow are absent.

evidence.target: final exact-head memory + Windows + Ubuntu CI
evidence.note: This normal user commit triggers the authoritative final matrix.

limitations: The aggregate durable-root 64 MiB quota remains #89 and is intentionally implemented next on top of this committed format.
POSIX mode bits secure plugin-created files; the user-supplied durableRoot itself is not destructively chmodded, and Windows relies on platform ownership/ACL semantics rather than POSIX mode claims.
